_comment: The /bay places. GeoJSON points with a first-person note each: what it is, why it matters, what happened there. Never a bare pin. Coordinates are [lng, lat]; categories are the layer enum in assets/bay/map.js. Add places freely, keep the notes honest and yours.

properties.name: advanceiq · the day job
properties.note: the day job. i'm the sole engineer on ARIA, an llm agent that lets revenue-based-finance clients query analytics in plain english. mastra, next.js, a custom sse layer. this dot is the block i walk to every morning.

properties.name: wingmic · the coffee shop build
properties.note: my side project. speak for 10 to 30 seconds after meeting someone and an llm turns it into a knowledge graph you can query in plain english, mcp server included. most of it got written at a table around here.

properties.name: south park
properties.note: a lawn in the middle of soma that has watched two booms. multimedia gulch started in the houses around it, and now it's ai pitch decks at every picnic table. i bring lunch here when i want to overhear the future.

properties.name: moscone west
properties.note: the hackathon floor. my first sf weekend was a 36 hour build here on folding tables; i left with a working demo and a cold. the startup scene shows up whenever there's free compute.

properties.name: the googleplex
properties.note: the mothership down the peninsula. a friend gave me the tour: the bikes are real, the campus is bigger than some sf neighborhoods, and the cafeterias justify the commute all by themselves.

properties.name: apple park
properties.note: the ring, seen from the visitor center. the scale model inside is better than walking the real thing, which is the most apple sentence i've ever written.

properties.name: 1 hacker way
properties.note: the thumbs-up sign over the lawn. i detoured past on a 101 ride to menlo park; the campus is a small city that ships one app.

properties.name: salesforce tower
properties.note: the tallest thing downtown and my compass since i moved here. the crown runs a nightly led piece; on a clear evening you can pick it out from the bay bridge.

properties.name: the mission
properties.note: the house hunt ended here, two blocks off valencia. taquerias, fog that rolls in around 7 like a scheduled deploy, and a commute i can do in sneakers.

properties.name: the sunset
properties.note: runner-up in the house hunt. quiet, flat, parking that actually exists. the fog is honest about staying until noon, and my budget liked it more than my alarm did.

properties.name: the richmond
properties.note: the in-between neighborhood: golden gate park on one side, the presidio on the other. rent is saner, the fog is not. third place in the hunt, first place for pho.

properties.name: 4th & king caltrain
properties.note: the caltrain decision. live near this platform and every peninsula office becomes a one seat ride. still the tiebreaker for the next apartment.

properties.name: oracle park
properties.note: the giants' ballpark where a home run can land in the bay. bleacher seats are the cheapest the city gets, and the view is part of the ticket.

properties.name: chase center
properties.note: warriors home across the water from the ballpark. the arena reads like a spaceship parked next to the older stadiums; the ferry there is half the fun.

properties.name: kezar stadium
properties.note: a public track at the east edge of golden gate park. tuesday intervals here beat any gym membership, and the fog keeps the legs honest.

properties.name: golden gate bridge
properties.note: the first real walk i took after the move. the bridge is louder than you think, the wind is a wall, and some mornings the fog eats it whole anyway.

properties.name: ferry building
properties.note: the clock tower you set your bearings by. saturday farmers market; the bakery line moves faster than it looks and it's worth it.

properties.name: sutro baths
properties.note: the ruins of a swimming palace at the edge of the continent. best sunset per dollar in sf, and the dollar is zero.

properties.name: twin peaks
properties.note: the whole street grid at your feet. bring a layer no matter the forecast; the wind up there is a feature, not a bug.

properties.name: bernal heights summit
properties.note: a 360 of the city and dogs everywhere. my default answer to 'where do i go to think', and the walk up counts as the gym.

properties.name: alamo square
properties.note: the postcard houses with downtown behind them. tour groups at 10am, locals at sunset, and the lawn in between earned its reputation.

properties.name: palace of fine arts
properties.note: built for the 1915 world's fair and kept alive because people refused to let it go. weeping concrete, swans, the best echo in the city.

properties.name: chinatown dragon gate
properties.note: the gate on grant street. walk uphill, get a pastry, keep going past the souvenir shops until the aunties are selling produce on the sidewalk.
